GR1.claim: GoaMiles, the app-based taxi service promoted by Goa Tourism, books cabs anywhere in the state; an airport shuttle bus also runs from outside the airport.

evidence.quote: You can now book a cab via the Goa Miles App.
you can book a cab to any destination across the State
The shuttle bus departs from outside the airport premises.

GR2.claim: River ferries run from dawn till late evening and are free for pedestrians and two-wheelers.

evidence.quote: they are extremely reasonable and run from dawn till late in the evening
It’s free for pedestrians and two wheelers and minimal charges are applicable to cars.

GR3.claim: Private local buses reach even remote areas and are the cheapest way around; read the route on the board in the front window. State-run KTC buses run the main routes.

evidence.quote: Local private buses in Goa have a wide network even in the remotest areas.
You can find out the route from the sign board on the front window.
State run services, KTC ply on major routes and cities.

GR4.claim: GTDC lists scooter hire at about ₹200–500 a day and geared bikes ₹400–1,000, depending on bike and season — check current rates.

evidence.quote: The price range is Rs. 200 to Rs. 350 even Rs 500 per day depending on the kind of bike and season. Geared bikes range from Rs. 400 to Rs. 1000 per day.

GR5.claim: Airport pre-paid taxis charge a standard fare by distance.

evidence.quote: You can avail of the pre-paid taxi service from the airport that follows a standard amount based on number of kilometers.

GR6.claim: Trains stop at Thivim, Karmali, Madgaon and Vasco da Gama; Madgaon is about 38 km from Panaji.

evidence.quote: Trains depart from Thivim, Karmali, Madgaon and Vasco da Gama at regular intervals.
Madgaon railway station is about 38 km away from Panaji

GR7.claim: Panaji to Margao is about 35 km — around an hour in traffic.

evidence.quote: From Panaji to Margao city, the commercial capital is around 35kms and can take around an hour to get there if you get traffic along the way.

GR8.claim: The UNESCO monuments are free to enter; most museums charge a small fee.

evidence.quote: Most of the museums have a small fee, but the UNESCO monuments are free to enter.

GR9.claim: Fontainhas and Old Goa's UNESCO sites can be walked at an easy pace, and Ponda's temples are easy to reach from any city.

evidence.quote: A leisurely  stroll through Fontainhas or a walk to the UNESCO Heritage sites in Old Goa can easily be  enjoyed at your own  pace.
Ponda taluka is a buzzing religious destination with its  famous temples and can be easily accessed from any city.

PJ2.claim: Panaji's landmark church, built in 1619, is known for its double flight of stairs added in 1871.

evidence.quote: The present church, with its Baroque façade framed by twin towers, was built in 1619. Its most striking feature, the double flight of stairs leading up to the church, was added in 1871.

PJ5.claim: The Fontainhas quarter has narrow lanes and colourful houses.

evidence.quote: Explore the Fontainhas neighbourhood with its narrow lanes and colourful houses

PJ7.claim: Miramar, 3 km from Panaji at the mouth of the Mandovi, is a family city beach with a view of Fort Aguada.

evidence.quote: This beautiful ‘urban’ beach, akin to Chowpatty in Mumbai, is located just 3 kms from Panaji.

OG4.claim: Old Goa is about 9 km east of Panaji, where the viceroy moved in 1759.

evidence.quote: he removed himself and his government to the future capital, Panjim (then a village about 9 kilometres to the west)

evidence.quote: This long, seven-km sweep of sand located 15 kms from Panaji, is called the ‘Queen of Beaches’.

PJ6.claim: Dabolim airport is about 30 km from Panaji and Mopa about 40 km; the Kadamba bus stand at Patto is the city's bus hub.

evidence.quote: The nearest airport is Dabolim Airport which is 30 kilometres (19 miles) away.
KTC Bus Stand, Patto, Panjim is Panjim's central bus stand

evidence.quote: The tourist season in Goa is from October to March and is at its peak from December to February

GS23.claim: Don't swim in the sea during the monsoon.

evidence.quote: Do not swim in the monsoon.

which is brought down once every 10 years.

guides.seoDescription: Getting to Goa: Mopa vs Dabolim airport, Margao, Thivim, Karmali and Vasco stations, Kadamba buses from Mumbai, NH-66, and booking tips for peak season.

body.intro: Goa is small, but it has two airports about 60 km apart and four main railway stations. Pick the one nearest where you will stay — the north and south coasts are an hour or more apart.

items.body: In Pernem, North Goa, open since January 2023 — about 40 km from Panaji and closest to the northern beaches.
items.title: Mopa (Manohar International)

items.body: A civil enclave at the naval base INS Hansa near Vasco da Gama, about 30 km from Panaji — better for Panaji and the south.
items.title: Dabolim

items.body: Flights run full from October to January.
items.title: Book early

items.body: Pre-paid taxis charge a standard fare by distance; an airport shuttle bus leaves from outside the terminal; or book a GoaMiles cab.
items.title: From the airport

items.body: Trains stop at Thivim, Karmali, Madgaon and Vasco da Gama. Madgaon Junction, on the Konkan Railway, is about 38 km from Panaji.
items.title: Stations

items.body: About 8–12 hours. Trains often run full — reserve well ahead.
items.title: From Mumbai

items.body: NH-66 runs along the coast to Mumbai and Mangalore; NH-4A climbs to Belagavi.
items.title: Highways

items.body: Kadamba Transport Corporation and private operators run interstate buses from the Kadamba bus stand in Panaji; Mumbai is about 12–16 hours.
items.title: Buses

sections.heading: By sea
sections.text: There is no regular passenger ferry from Mumbai — the last sea service stopped in June 2004.

checklist: Pick Mopa for the north, Dabolim for Panaji and the south.

body.intro: Goa has no metro and few metered taxis, so plan how you'll move. Most travellers mix cabs, local buses and a hired scooter; river ferries are a free bonus.

items.body: Goa Tourism's app-based taxi service books cabs anywhere in the state.

items.body: Mapusa for the northern beaches, Margao for the south, the Kadamba stand in Panaji for everything else.

items.body: Traffic drives on the left; carry your licence and ID.

body.intro: Most Goa trips go wrong in the water or with the law. Goa Tourism's own do's and don'ts are short and worth following.

items.body: Swim only between the red-and-yellow flags watched by lifesavers; never where a red flag flies. Water sports stay inside the chequered flags.

items.body: Beaches are open 7 am to sunset.
items.title: Hours

items.body: Don't swim from June to September — the sea is rough with dangerous undercurrents.

items.title: Rocks

items.title: Alcohol and smoking

items.body: Non-bailable under the NDPS Act, with sentences from 6 months to 30 years.
items.title: Drugs

items.body: Dress modestly at temples, churches and mosques; nudity in public is illegal.

items.body: No vehicles on beaches. Traffic drives on the left.
items.title: Driving
